description: Automerge is the default posture here, not the exception. This repo is a design catalog with no downstream consumers: nothing depends on its artifacts, so a bad bump costs a revert, not a broken release. What stops a bad bump reaching main is the `Protect Main` ruleset — CI (build + discovery, unit tests, ktfmtCheck, catalog spec, catalog spec) is required, and `platformAutomerge` hands the merge to GitHub's own auto-merge, which only fires once those checks pass. Set the ruleset up with `scripts/setup-repo-protection.sh`; without it, automerge silently degrades to merging as soon as Renovate can, which is not what any of this intends.

packageRules.description: Majors are never automerged. A major on Kotlin, Compose Multiplatform or the preview toolchain changes what the catalog renders, and the render is the product — a human looks at the visual diff before it lands. Also hold a major for two weeks so the ecosystem's first round of regressions surfaces on someone else's CI.

Wear Compose and the mobile Compose BOM decide how every sticker in the catalog is laid out, and the render is the product — so they land as one PR whose visual diff is the review, not on automerge. Glance Wear is in the group because it is the third member of the Remote trio (AGENTS.md): it shares a `remote-creation*` base with `compose-remote` and `wear-compose-remote`, so a bump of it alone skews the trio and fails in the player at render time (#652).

Horologist is the catalog's SECOND component library (see AGENTS.md) and it ships its artifacts as one release — media-ui-material3, auth-composables-material3, compose-layout, images-base and the models they take all move together, and a skew between them is a compile error at best. Group them into one PR. Not automerged, for the same reason Compose is not: these draw the media player, the sign-in screens and the fast-scrolling list, and the render is the product — a human reads the visual diff. They are on an alpha line, so expect the diff to be real.

Toolchain and CI plumbing — the Gradle wrapper, the GitHub Actions pins and the pinned Node version. These are judged entirely by whether CI passes, which is the one thing automerge already waits for, so batch them into a single weekly PR rather than one PR per action. Deliberately BEFORE the compose-ai-tools rule, which re-claims its own action ref out of this batch — that pin travels with the Gradle coords, not with the weekly plumbing.

Published modules are versionless and resolve through their release BOMs. Keep synthetic source-composite coordinates disabled; the BOM rules below re-enable published BOM updates. The daemon alignment check rejects a BOM older than the plugin runtime floor.

Keep the Gradle plugin marker and pinned reusable action/workflow refs on the same compose-ai-tools release. The daemon BOM updates independently and must meet the plugin runtime floor checked by verifyComposePreviewDaemonAlignment.
Re-enable the UI-builder release BOM after the module rule. The exporter resolves through this BOM and is verified by WearScreenTemplateRoundTripTest.
